reuse.why: Fintegra reuses the Akahu link function and a newly extracted downloadSingleProviderTransactions, and takeover reuses unlinkAccount, rather than writing new copies of those flows.

duplication.why: The link guard is defined once in prepareBankAccountLink, but six near-identical inline wrappers repeat 'prepare then link' at registration instead of one higher-order wrapper; the pre-existing per-provider link copies remain.

placement.why: Link rules are enforced in app.method registration wrappers outside the link functions, and Fintegra is folded into linkAkahuAccount through provider ternaries rather than a provider-neutral link helper.

scope.why: Mostly focused on the four steps; the DbAccount sync-source union fix and download refactor are related, though unlinkAccount's new 'ok' return path is inconsistent with its other paths.

maintainability.why: Central guard is easy to follow, but linkAkahuAccount now carries Fintegra special cases and unlinkAccount a mode flag, and each new provider needs another hand-written wrapper.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All six link requests go through prepareBankAccountLink and findOrCreateBank; the takeover goes through unlinkAccount.

disguised_duplication.where: The registration wrappers are plain visible repeats, and the Akahu download body was genuinely extracted and shared.

abstraction_drift.where: accounts/app.ts linkAkahuAccount gains a provider parameter with Fintegra branches for the bank key (orgId vs orgDomain) and sync-event tables; unlinkAccount gains preserveProviderConnection with an early-return branch.
